learning_outcomes.text: Recognize and understand the general laws of applied physics (mechanics, thermodynamics, fields and waves, and electromagnetism) that apply to engineering
Apply the general laws of mechanics, thermodynamics, fields and waves, and electromagnetism to solve problems typical of engineering
Recognize and understand the training needs that will be useful to successfully solve new situations related to industrial engineering
Propose creative solutions to satisfactorily respond to real needs and problems of society
Develop professional texts and scientific-technical reports according to the conventions of the field of industrial technical engineering
Adapt the organization of content and the use of language, verbal and non-verbal, to argue in diverse situations or before diverse audiences
Apply knowledge specific to industrial engineering in the learning of new methods and theories
Show the advantages and opportunities of different solutions to the same problem critically and constructively
Apply the principles and methods of quality

syllabus_topics: Degrees of freedom and equations of motion
Dry friction forces and resistive forces
Curvilinear motion and intrinsic axes of motion
Newton's laws in rotating reference frames
Dynamics of Systems of Several Bodies ("Particles")
Moments of forces and angular momentum
Particular case: Rotation in the plane of a rigid body and moment of inertia
Hooke's Law and linearization of the equations of motion
Harmonic oscillators in one and two dimensions
Examples of nonlinear systems and chaotic response
Calculus of variations and Euler-Lagrange equations
Variational formulation of Mechanics and Hamilton's Principle
General (3-D) Dynamics of the Rigid Body
Rotation of the rigid body with a fixed axis
Rotation of the rigid body with a fixed point
Rotation of the rigid body about the center of mass
Translation and rotation of the rigid body
teaching_methods: Problem/exercise solving in the ordinary classroom
assessment_rules: Evaluation by means of exercises posed and performed in the classroom throughout the semester for practical cases. Evaluation by means of a written exam at the end of the semester for mixed tests. Further details may be found in other comments.
